main_logic: Hail is measured as hazard's MESH75 hail diameter, in mm.
Published hail-damage thresholds by roofing material (onset and full failure) turned into a replacement probability, times the roof's share of building cost.
The damage ratio is a share of each part's own replacement value (roof cover; walls and windows).

steps.name: What it covers
steps.meaning: The parts that have a curve, their share of the value, and what has none yet
steps.fact: 6 parts with a curve · 1 without one yet
paragraphs: Hail on buildings: published hail-damage thresholds by roofing material (onset and full failure) turned into a replacement probability, times the roof's share of building cost. It names 6 parts: House roof (asphalt shingles), Warehouse roof (standing-seam steel), Office roof (TPO membrane and insulation), House walls and windows, Warehouse windows and Office windows. Outside its scope: contents (declared as a withheld placeholder part) and wind and flooding from the same storm (other cells). Kinds of damage it does not include: rain entering after a roof breach, cosmetic denting and wear from repeated small hail.

For this hazard the building is split into 6 parts: House roof (asphalt shingles), Warehouse roof (standing-seam steel), Office roof (TPO membrane and insulation), House walls and windows, Warehouse windows and Office windows. 2 further units are named but withheld — hre exposed equipment and hre building contents — a stated 'not zero', not a curve. Parts of the plant's value with no curve yet: outdoor equipment: AC condenser, rooftop units (whether it sits in the profile value is an open question).

The damage ratio is a share of each part's own replacement value (roof cover; walls and windows); building share = unit damage x the part's share of structure replacement cost. The files state no plant-level dollar figure for this asset.

sources.locator: Abstract and §1 p. 1 (asphalt shingles about 80% of US residential roof coverings; repeated sub-severe hail lowers the shingles' resistance to later large hail and speeds aging)

sources.citation: Ezold, R. (Vertex). HVAC condenser coil hail damage — repair or replace? Vertex web article, 22 May 2018, citing ASME IMECE2007-41518 'Hail effects on air conditioner performance'.
sources.locator: Web article: coils with 41% of fin area flattened had little or no capacity loss (SEER -2 to -5%); 100% flattened lost 23-27% of capacity; combing restored units to within 1-4% of undented capacity
sources.permitted: Support withholding the exposed-equipment unit: fin denting is mostly cosmetic or comb-repairable; functional damage needs evidence not found.
sources.prohibited: Read as a hail-size threshold or a repair-cost ratio; read as evidence of zero damage.

claims.text: Field surveys put the onset of hail damage at 1.00 in for three-tab asphalt shingles and 1.25 in for laminated shingles (all ages).
claims.update_trigger: A US claims study by roof type and hail size.

claims.text: Freezer ice stones at free-fall speed, perpendicular impacts: 11-year-old laminated shingles were damaged by 0/0/60/90/100% of impacts at 1/1.25/1.5/1.75/2.0 in; 11-year-old three-tab fiberglass shingles by 0/60/90/100/100%.
claims.locator: p. 3 Table 2; p. 2 (test ice harder than natural hail; perpendicular = worst case)

claims.text: Roofing damage means a diminished water-shedding capability or a reduced expected life (shingle punctures, tears, mat fractures, granules displaced to expose the bitumen); granule loss alone is not functional damage.
claims.locator: S001 p. 3 §4a; S002 text; S013 text

claims.text: Smallest hail sizes that damage low-slope coverings: thermoplastic single-ply membranes 1 to 2 in; EPDM 2 in; steel panels 2 1/2 in (hard hail, perpendicular impacts, average support, good or midlife roofs).
claims.locator: Figure 'Hail thresholds for low-slope roof coverings'
claims.parameter_or_rule: office roof band; warehouse roof onset
claims.update_trigger: A TPO hail test series by age and attachment.

claims.text: Metal panels in good to fair condition need hail of at least 2.5 in to rupture; dents on seam tops are not an open seam; insurers write cosmetic-damage exclusions.
claims.locator: S003 web article; S004 web page (metal cosmetic damage from 1.5 in)
claims.update_trigger: Haag 2010 report or a metal-panel hail test with sizes above 2.5 in.

claims.text: Single-ply membranes can be damaged by hail of 1.5 in or more; walls have no industry hail rating; glazing is susceptible (no size given).
claims.parameter_or_rule: cross-check; wall and window evidence gap

claims.text: Aged (up to 20-30-year equivalence) fully adhered 60-mil TPO on a high-density polyiso cover board was not punctured by 2 in ice balls unless struck over a fastener; cover boards cracked at 20-year equivalence after three impacts.
claims.update_trigger: Hazard states the TPO attachment and cover board.

claims.text: Hazus default one-storey residential subassembly cost ratios: roofing 3% of building cost; repair work costs 1.25 times new work (repair-and-remodel factor).
claims.update_trigger: A published US cost model by component.

claims.text: Hazus replaces the whole asphalt roof covering once more than 0.5% of it is damaged.
Hazus three-storey motel cost ratios: roof covering 1.1%, roof insulation 0.7% (roofing 2.1%); commercial repair factor 1.25 and overhead and profit 1.20.
Hazus adjusts commercial roofing cost ratios by storey count: R' = R(1 - 2.2(Nm/N - 1)) for fewer storeys.

Reference designs: house asphalt shingles on wood sheathing, 6:12 gable, roof 2,218.18 ft2, vinyl siding, windows 15%; warehouse standing-seam metal, 1:12, roof 100,346.62 ft2, insulated metal walls, windows 2%, eight overhead doors; office TPO on insulated metal deck, roof 18,003.91 ft2, masonry veneer, windows 33%, six rooftop units; roof covers 10 years old; budgets $405,000, $11.0M, $10.8M.

Hazard sends mesh_diameter_mm = MESH75 = 15.096 x ((raw/2.54)^2)^0.206 (capped at 203.2 mm) for native pixels with raw MRMS MESH >= 25.4 mm and zero damage elsewhere; MESH75 at raw 25.4 mm is 38.98 mm.
claims.update_trigger: Hazard changes the transform or adds a ground-truth bridge.

claims.text: Swiss insured buildings: mean damage ratio 0.05% (CI 0.02-0.09%) of building value at 60 mm MESHS, with 5% of buildings claiming.
Asphalt shingles cover about 80% of US homes; repeated sub-severe hail lowers shingle resistance to later large hail.
Flattening 41% of condenser fins barely changes capacity; combing restores units to within 1-4% of undented capacity.
claims.update_trigger: Equipment hail damage evidence by size.

claims.text: NRI hail building expected annual loss rate (hail_ealb / hail_expb) on Hazard's grid: median 1.4e-5 per year, 95th percentile 2.1e-4, maximum 2.8e-3.
The legacy Real Estate_Hail array (Schmid-derived, centimetre grid relabelled as inches, plateau about 5.78%) is rejected for runtime use.
Hazus has no hail model, and no published US building hail vulnerability curve was found.
claims.update_trigger: A published US building hail vulnerability study.

claims.text: Each part's onset and full-damage sizes are read as the 5th and 95th percentiles of the size that makes it need replacing (lognormal), as the convective real-estate cell reads EF bounds.
The standing-seam roof is fully failed by 3.5 in (95%).
The warehouse roof panels are 12% of the warehouse's replacement cost (range 9-15%).
claims.update_trigger: A published metal-roof replacement rate (e.g. a cost book).

claims.text: Walls and windows (T4): vinyl siding band 1.25-2.0 in, half of it on hail-facing elevations; window glass band 1.5-2.5 in, a quarter of panes reached; costs $7/ft2 siding, $55/ft2 residential and $80/ft2 commercial window.
claims.update_trigger: Any wall or window hail study.

claims.text: Cosmetic denting (metal roof, metal wall panels, overhead doors, gutters) and fin denting are not physical loss of function and are outside the y-axis.
